To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the use of OO metrics to evaluate the quality of component-based applications is feasible, (2) the use of some OO metrics is more relevant to evaluate the quality than the use of others, (3) the use of the OSGi framework leads to a better respect of properties pointed out by component-based software engineering community than the use of traditional object-oriented programming.
(1) the OO metrics are useful to evaluate OSGi applications and (2) the OSGi developers respect most of the properties pointed out by literature.

1) the use of OO metrics is relevant for the quality evaluation of OSGi component-based applications, 2) the use of OSGi metrics is relevant for this evaluation too, and 3) the use of both OO metrics and OSGi metrics allows to better evaluate the quality of these kind of applications than only the use of OO or OSGi metrics.
